title: Getting started with midasINLA
text: midasINLA allows regression coefficient βi\beta_i vary across spatial units two ways: Spatially structured coefficient: βi=β*+bi,𝒃∼iCAR⁡(τb,𝑾),   \beta_i = \beta^* + b_i, \qquad   \boldsymbol{b} \sim \operatorname{iCAR}(\tau_b,\mathbf{W}),    β*\beta^* overall effect bib_i represents spatially structured deviation unit ii. deviations follow intrinsic conditional autoregressive (iCAR) model precision τb\tau_b spatial weights matrix 𝑾\mathbf{W}, subject sum--zero constraint ∑ibi=0\sum_i b_i=0. Unstructured coefficient: βi∼iidN(0,σβ2),   \beta_i \overset{iid}{\sim}   N(0,\sigma_\beta^2),    coefficients independent across spatial units. constant coefficient, βi≡β\beta_i\equiv\beta, also supported corresponds special case effect across spatial units.

title: Getting started with midasINLA
text: lag weights obtained normalising constraint function ψ(𝜸,k)\psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k): wk=h(𝜸,k)=ψ(𝜸,k)∑j=0Kψ(𝜸,j). w_k = h(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k) = \frac{\psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k)} {\sum_{j=0}^K \psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},j)}. midasINLA implements several commonly used constraint functions. Exponential Almon polynomial (order 2): ψ(𝜸,k)=exp⁡(∑j=12γjkj), \psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k) = \exp\left(\sum_{j=1}^{2}\gamma_j k^j\right), 𝜸=(γ1,γ2)\boldsymbol{\gamma}=(\gamma_1,\gamma_2). Beta polynomial: ψ(𝜸,k)=xkγ1−1(1−xk)γ2−1, \psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k) = x_k^{\gamma_1-1}(1-x_k)^{\gamma_2-1}, xk=ξ+(1−2ξ)kK, x_k=\xi+(1-2\xi)\frac{k}{K}, ξ>0\xi>0 small fixed constant 𝜸=(γ1,γ2)\boldsymbol{\gamma}=(\gamma_1,\gamma_2). one-parameter version obtained fixing γ1=1\gamma_1=1. Hyperbolic scheme: ψ(γ,k)=Γ(k+γ)Γ(k+1)Γ(γ), \psi(\gamma,k) = \frac{\Gamma(k+\gamma)}{\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(\gamma)},  γ>0\gamma>0. Gaussian kernel: ψ(𝜸,k)=exp⁡{−(k−γ1)22γ2}. \psi(\boldsymbol{\gamma},k)=\exp\left\{-\frac{(k-\gamma_1)^2}{2\gamma_2}\right\}. 𝜸=(γ1,γ2)\boldsymbol{\gamma}=(\gamma_1,\gamma_2) γ2>0\gamma_2>0.

title: Getting started with midasINLA
text: MIDAS lag structure incorporated latent Gaussian model INLA’s rgeneric interface. MIDAS constraint functions define lag weights function low-dimensional parameter vector, resulting weighted high-frequency covariates represented part latent model. functions midasINLA construct required rgeneric model components interface INLA::inla(). allows MIDAS lag-weight parameters regression coefficients estimated within INLA framework, retaining spatial structure specified regression coefficients. Users need construct rgeneric model directly; handled internally package functions demonstrated . example illustrates main functions midasINLA: prepare_Minla_spatial() prepares high-frequency covariates inclusion model; fit_Minla_spatial() fits resulting model using INLA; compute_beta_spatial() obtains posterior summaries regression coefficients; compute_weights() obtains posterior summaries MIDAS lag weights; predict_midas() generates posterior predictions.

code: res_weights <- compute_weights(fit_res) head(res_weights$hf_1) #>   lag       mean       q2.5      q97.5 #> 1   0 0.04550320 0.04371408 0.04766043 #> 2   1 0.04082168 0.03979364 0.04204024 #> 3   2 0.03872292 0.03800923 0.03956152 #> 4   3 0.03739603 0.03687296 0.03800647 #> 5   4 0.03643514 0.03604624 0.03688603 #> 6   5 0.03568627 0.03539969 0.03601610 head(res_weights$hf_2) #>   lag       mean       q2.5      q97.5 #> 1   0 0.03018182 0.02873091 0.03160778 #> 2   1 0.03209143 0.03063139 0.03349881 #> 3   2 0.03389293 0.03234583 0.03521736 #> 4   3 0.03555531 0.03395167 0.03684984 #> 5   4 0.03704881 0.03558236 0.03833785 #> 6   5 0.03834579 0.03690312 0.03957650 ggplot(res_weights$hf_1, aes(x = lag, y = mean)) +   geom_errorbar(     aes(       ymin = q2.5,       ymax = q97.5     ),     width = 0.2,     colour = "grey30"   ) +   geom_point(     aes(       colour = "Posterior mean"     ),     size = 2   ) +   geom_point(     aes(       y = data_spatialpoisson_example$weights1,       colour = "True value"     ),     size = 2   ) +   scale_colour_manual(     name = NULL,     values = c(       "Posterior mean" = "red",       "True value" = "blue"     )   ) +   labs(     x = "Lag",     y = "Lag weight"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom"   ) ggplot(res_weights$hf_2, aes(x = lag, y = mean)) +   geom_errorbar(     aes(       ymin = q2.5,       ymax = q97.5     ),     width = 0.2,     colour = "grey30"   ) +   geom_point(     aes(       colour = "Posterior mean"     ),     size = 2   ) +   geom_point(     aes(       y = data_spatialpoisson_example$weights2,       colour = "True value"     ),     size = 2   ) +   scale_colour_manual(     name = NULL,     values = c(       "Posterior mean" = "red",       "True value" = "blue"     )   ) +   labs(     x = "Lag",     y = "Lag weight"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom"   )

title: Getting started with midasINLA
text: final 10 time points withheld model fit used illustrate posterior prediction. Posterior predictions can generated using predict_midas(): returned object contains posterior summaries predicted outcome, including posterior means 95% credible intervals, well posterior samples latent predictor. posterior summaries predicted outcome can accessed using: predicted observed outcomes can also compared graphically. following example shows results first four spatial locations. dashed vertical line indicates boundary training held-prediction periods.
code: pred_res <- predict_midas(   model = fit_res,   family = "poisson",   Ntrials = NULL,   nsamples = 1000 ) head(pred_res$computed_y$mean) #> [1] 92.129 20.611 54.692 76.626 14.775 11.992 head(pred_res$computed_y$q2.5) #> [1] 74 12 41 60  8  6 head(pred_res$computed_y$q97.5) #> [1] 112.000  30.000  69.000  93.025  23.000  19.000 plot_data <- data.frame(   observed = fit_res$data_final$y_all,   predicted = pred_res$computed_y$mean,   lower = pred_res$computed_y$q2.5,   upper = pred_res$computed_y$q97.5,   loc = fit_res$data_final$loc,   Time = fit_res$data_final$Time )  plot_long <- plot_data |>   dplyr::filter(loc %in% 1:4) |>   tidyr::pivot_longer(     cols = c(observed, predicted),     names_to = "series",     values_to = "value"   )  # Determine the training/held-out boundary for each location non_na <- !is.na(fit_res$data_final$y)  segment <- cumsum(   non_na != dplyr::lag(non_na, default = TRUE) ) segment[!non_na] <- NA  rel_idx <- ave(   seq_along(non_na),   segment,   FUN = seq_along )  first_na <- which(   diff(c(FALSE, is.na(fit_res$data_final$y))) == 1 )  vlines <- data.frame(   cut = rel_idx[first_na - 1] + 1,   loc = seq_len(16) ) |>   dplyr::filter(loc %in% 1:4)  ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = Time, y = value, colour = series)) +   geom_ribbon(     data = plot_data |>       dplyr::filter(loc %in% 1:4),     aes(       x = Time,       ymin = lower,       ymax = upper     ),     inherit.aes = FALSE,     fill = "red",     alpha = 0.2   ) +   geom_line() +   geom_vline(     data = vlines,     aes(xintercept = cut),     colour = "black",     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   facet_wrap(     ~loc,     ncol = 2,     labeller = labeller(       loc = function(x) paste("Loc =", x)     )   ) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c(       "observed" = "blue",       "predicted" = "red"     )   ) +   labs(     x = "Time",     y = "Outcome",     colour = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom"   )

title: Spatial MIDAS Models Using INLA
text: package includes spatial Poisson dataset illustrating main modelling workflow. typical analysis involves preparing high-frequency covariates, fitting spatial MIDAS model, obtaining posterior summaries.
code: library(midasINLA) library(INLA)  data("data_spatialpoisson_example")  # Read the spatial adjacency graph g <- INLA::inla.read.graph(   filename = system.file("map.adj", package = "midasINLA") )  # Prepare the first high-frequency covariate Midas_x1 <- prepare_Minla_spatial(   x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$x1,   loc_x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$loc,   constraint = "hyperbolic",   K = 0:29,   m = 30,   svc = TRUE,   svc_prior = "icar",   g = g )  # Prepare the second high-frequency covariate Midas_x2 <- prepare_Minla_spatial(   x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x2$x2,   loc_x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x2$loc,   constraint = "gaussian",   K = 0:45,   m = 30,   svc = FALSE )  # Fit the model fit_res <- fit_Minla_spatial(   formula = y ~ 1,   hf_input = list(Midas_x1, Midas_x2),   data = response_data,   loc_var = "loc",   time_var = "Time",   family = "poisson",   inla_options = list(     verbose = FALSE,     num.threads = 1,     control.predictor = list(       compute = TRUE,       link = 1     )   ) )

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {   INLA::inla.setOption(num.threads = 1)    data(data_spatialpoisson_example)    # Read the spatial adjacency graph   g <- INLA::inla.read.graph(     filename = system.file("map.adj", package = "midasINLA")   )    # Prepare a spatial MIDAS predictor   Midas_x1 <- prepare_Minla_spatial(     x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$x1,     loc_x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$loc,     constraint = "hyperbolic",     K = 0:29,     m = 30,     svc = TRUE,     svc_prior = "icar",     g = g   )    # Fit the spatial Poisson MIDAS model   fit <- fit_Minla_spatial(     formula = y ~ 1,     data = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_y,     loc_var = "loc",     time_var = "Time",     family = "poisson",     hf_input = list(Midas_x1),     inla_options = list(       verbose = FALSE,       control.predictor = list(         compute = TRUE,         link = 1       )     )   )    # Compute posterior summaries of the MIDAS coefficients   beta_summary <- compute_beta_spatial(     model = fit,     n_loc = 16   )    # Inspect summaries of the location-specific total coefficients   beta_summary$hf_index_1$summary.total.beta } } # }

text: Fits Mixed Data Sampling (MIDAS) regression model optional spatially varying coefficients using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). High-frequency covariates supplied MIDAS objects created prepare_Minla_spatial().

title: Fit a spatial MIDAS model using INLA — fit_Minla_spatial
code: fit_Minla_spatial(   formula,   data,   loc_var,   time_var,   family,   hf_input = NULL,   Ntrials = NULL,   E = NULL,   inla_options = list() )

title: Fit a spatial MIDAS model using INLA — fit_Minla_spatial
text: formula model formula specifying response covariates. response variable must column data. data data frame containing response additional model covariates. must contain variables specified loc_var time_var. loc_var Character string specifying name location variable data. time_var Character string specifying name time variable data. family Character string specifying likelihood family response. example, "poisson" "binomial". hf_input list MIDAS objects returned prepare_Minla_spatial(). object specifies high-frequency covariate MIDAS lag structure. Multiple MIDAS objects can supplied. Ntrials Optional vector specifying number trials binomial response. Used family = "binomial". E Optional vector expected counts exposure values Poisson model. length must match number rows data. Used family = "poisson". inla_options named list additional arguments passed INLA::inla(). default, control.compute$config set TRUE already specified.

title: Fit a spatial MIDAS model using INLA — fit_Minla_spatial
text: list containing: formula_final final INLA model formula, including MIDAS components. data_final response data used model fitting ordering location time removing rows incomplete lagged covariate information. rm_max maximum number initial observations removed across locations incomplete MIDAS lagged covariates. res fitted INLA model returned INLA::inla(). hf_input list MIDAS objects supplied hf_input.

title: Fit a spatial MIDAS model using INLA — fit_Minla_spatial
text: function constructs INLA model incorporating MIDAS components specified hf_input. Multiple high-frequency covariates can included supplying multiple MIDAS objects hf_input.

title: Fit a spatial MIDAS model using INLA — fit_Minla_spatial
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {   data(data_spatialpoisson_example)    # Read the spatial adjacency graph   g <- INLA::inla.read.graph(     filename = system.file("map.adj", package = "midasINLA")   )    # Prepare a spatial MIDAS predictor   Midas_x1 <- prepare_Minla_spatial(     x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$x1,     loc_x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$loc,     constraint = "hyperbolic",     K = 0:29,     m = 30,     svc = TRUE,     svc_prior = "icar",     g = g   )    # Fit the spatial Poisson MIDAS model   fit <- fit_Minla_spatial(     formula = y ~ 1,     data = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_y,     loc_var = "loc",     time_var = "Time",     family = "poisson",     hf_input = list(Midas_x1),     inla_options = list(       verbose = FALSE,       control.predictor = list(         compute = TRUE,         link = 1       )     )   )    # Inspect the fitted INLA model   fit$res } } # }

what: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
text: Generates posterior predictive samples fitted MIDAS model using posterior samples latent linear predictor. function supports Gaussian, Poisson, binomial response distributions.

title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
code: predict_midas(model, family = "gaussian", Ntrials = NULL, nsamples = 1000)

title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
text: model fitted MIDAS model returned fit_Minla_spatial(). family Character string specifying likelihood family. Supported values "gaussian", "poisson", "binomial". Defaults "gaussian". Ntrials Optional vector specifying number trials observation family = "binomial". omitted, function attempts use Ntrials column model$data_final. nsamples Positive integer specifying number posterior samples used generate predictive distribution. Defaults 1000.

title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
text: list two components: computed_y list containing posterior predictive summaries: mean Posterior predictive mean observation. sd Posterior predictive standard deviation observation. q2.5 2.5% posterior predictive quantile observation. q97.5 97.5% posterior predictive quantile observation. samples list containing posterior samples latent predictor , Gaussian responses, posterior samples observation variance.

title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
text: Gaussian response, posterior samples observation variance obtained posterior samples Gaussian precision parameter used generate predictive observations. Poisson binomial responses, observations generated using appropriate inverse-link function.

title: Generate posterior predictive samples from a MIDAS model — predict_midas
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {   data(data_spatialpoisson_example)    Midas_x1 <- prepare_Minla_spatial(     x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$x1,     loc_x = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_x1$loc,     constraint = "hyperbolic",     K = 0:29,     m = 30,     svc = FALSE   )    fit <- fit_Minla_spatial(     formula = y ~ 1,     data = data_spatialpoisson_example$data_y,     loc_var = "loc",     time_var = "Time",     family = "poisson",     hf_input = list(Midas_x1),     inla_options = list(verbose = FALSE)   )    predictions <- predict_midas(     model = fit,     family = "poisson",     nsamples = 1000   )    # Inspect posterior predictive summaries   head(predictions$computed_y$mean)   head(predictions$computed_y$q2.5)   head(predictions$computed_y$q97.5) } } # }

what: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
title: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
text: Constructs MIDAS design matrix associated model specifications use fit_Minla_spatial(). function creates lagged high-frequency covariate values location optionally specifies spatially varying coefficient (SVC) component.

title: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
code: prepare_Minla_spatial(   x,   loc_x,   constraint,   K,   m,   svc = FALSE,   svc_prior = "iid",   g = NULL )

title: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
text: x Numeric vector high-frequency covariate observations. loc_x Vector identifying location associated observation x. length loc_x must equal length x. constraint Character string specifying constraint used MIDAS lag-response association. Supported constraints include "hyperbolic", "gaussian", "beta1", "beta2", "almon2". K Numeric vector specifying lags included MIDAS representation. m Numeric vector specifying number high-frequency covariate observations associated response observation. single value can supplied number observations constant time, vector can supplied number varies across response times. svc Logical; TRUE, specifies spatially varying coefficient model. Defaults FALSE. svc_prior Character string specifying prior spatially varying coefficient component. Must either "icar" "iid". Defaults "iid". g INLA graph object used "icar" prior. Required svc_prior = "icar".

title: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
text: list containing MIDAS design matrix model specifications. returned object includes: X_matrix MIDAS design matrix, including location index. constraint MIDAS constraint used lag-response association. lag_k maximum lag specified K. K vector lags used construct design matrix. m number high-frequency observations associated response observation. rm.row number initial rows removed location incomplete lagged observations. svc Whether spatially varying coefficient component specified. svc_prior prior specified spatially varying coefficient component. g INLA graph object, included svc_prior = "icar".

title: Prepare a spatial MIDAS object for INLA estimation — prepare_Minla_spatial
